name: CHROMEWORKS Spectre Null-Sig Covert Arm
product_name: Chromeworks Spectre Null-Signature Covert Operations Arm
description:
The Chromeworks Spectre is a full-arm replacement engineered for covert operation, built with signal-dampened servo housings that reduce acoustic signature to under 18 decibels during movement — quieter than a human wrist flexing. The chassis incorporates four hidden compartment bays distributed across the forearm and upper arm, accessible via neural-triggered dermis panels, capable of housing tools, data spikes, or compact sidearms without detection by standard security scanners due to a layered ceramic-polymer composite shell. Integrated micro-filament grapple and retractable pry-tool round out the covert toolkit without breaking the arm's clean profile.

The Spectre is the arm of choice for corporate intelligence operatives, licensed investigators working sensitive extraction contracts, and a significant portion of GLMZ's most expensive criminal talent. Chromeworks officially markets it to 'security professionals requiring discretion,' which is a polished way of saying they know exactly who is buying it and have structured their legal exposure accordingly. The hidden compartment feature technically crosses into Prohibited territory when used to carry concealed weapons, a fact that both buyers and Chromeworks prefer to leave unspoken.
installation_requirements: Full shoulder disarticulation, Chromeworks-certified secure installation facility, identity verification required at point of sale
rejection_risk: Low – ceramic-polymer composite housing reduces EMI interference with neural coupler; biocompatible wrist-socket lining standard
maintenance: Quarterly acoustic dampener servicing, compartment seal integrity check, firmware security updates

side_effects: Acoustic dampening requires continuous low-level neural signal suppression, causing mild tinnitus in approximately 18% of users
Compartment panel dermis can develop micro-tears under repeated high-speed access, requiring periodic resurfacing
Users report hypervigilance and difficulty relaxing the arm in non-operational settings — a conditioned response to covert operation training
Scanner-evasive shell occasionally interferes with medical imaging, complicating emergency treatment
cultural_context: In GLMZ's intelligence community, a Spectre arm is a known signal — it means you are either well-funded or well-connected, and probably both. The arm's presence at a social event is enough to make certain people quietly leave the room, and Chromeworks' marketing team has been careful never to acknowledge this reputation publicly while clearly cultivating it.
known_users: Corporate intelligence operatives and extraction specialists
Licensed private investigators working Tier 4-5 sensitive contracts
High-end professional criminals with access to Chromeworks' gray-market distribution
Off-books government operatives who need plausible civilian cover
Security consultants whose job descriptions are intentionally vague
story_hooks: A Spectre arm has been recovered at a crime scene with all four compartments emptied and the neural access logs wiped — forensics wants to know what was being carried
Chromeworks' certified installation records for Spectre units have been leaked, and several very powerful people are suddenly very nervous about who has that list
A player is offered a Spectre arm as payment for a job — the only catch is it's already registered to someone who was reported dead six months ago
